narrativeReportMd:
# BackboneElement R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard instance-validation break was found in the local `BackboneElement` element model: the canonical artifact, abstract flag, direct base, local `modifierExtension` cardinality, type, modifier flag, and summary flag are unchanged. The material issue is a runtime/code-generation hierarchy split: R6 introduces `BackboneType` and moves modifier-capable datatypes away from `BackboneElement` as their base.

## Scope
The report covers the core `BackboneElement` StructureDefinition plus the related R6 `BackboneType` artifact needed to assess whether `BackboneElement` was split. It excludes detailed concrete datatype migration and inherited Element/Extension changes, except where they explain the hierarchy split.

## Main migration themes
Instance JSON/XML for `BackboneElement.modifierExtension` is not locally tightened or renamed. Systems that generated model classes, reflection APIs, profile validators, or FHIRPath/type-dispatch logic assuming datatypes such as `Dosage`, `Timing`, or `ElementDefinition` are `BackboneElement` subclasses need to account for R6 `BackboneType`.

## Highest-impact findings
The single material finding is `BackboneElement:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:b7f4d2`: `BackboneElement` keeps its own shape but no longer owns the modifier-capable datatype branch in R6.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is recommended for downstream code generators and cross-version converters because the exact impact depends on whether they model FHIR abstract bases as classes, interfaces, traits, or metadata only.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The split appears conceptually justified because R6 distinguishes resource backbone elements from datatypes that can carry modifier extensions. A less disruptive design could have preserved a shared super-interface or alias for old generated APIs, but that would not remove the underlying semantic distinction.

## Follow-up analysis
Review `BackboneType`, `Extension`, `Element`, and each concrete datatype that changed base independently before final migration guidance is issued.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `BackboneElement` has no local element-level validation break, but R6 introduces `BackboneType` and shifts several modifier-capable datatypes out of the `BackboneElement` inheritance branch. The top concern is generated API/reflection/type-dispatch compatibility, not instance serialization. The main uncertainty is how official R6 migration guidance expects tooling to bridge the old and new hierarchy.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat R6 `BackboneElement` as the resource-backbone base and R6 `BackboneType` as the datatype-side replacement for R4 datatype bases that used `BackboneElement`. Migration should audit codegen templates, `instanceof` checks, validator type registries, profile derivation logic, and cross-version StructureDefinition conversion rules. JSON/XML instance payloads that only carry ordinary `modifierExtension` content are not made invalid by the local `BackboneElement` definition itself.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the direct StructureDefinition comparison and for the existence of the R6 `BackboneType` split, because these are explicit in local primary definitions. Overall confidence is medium because no official diff or narrative migration note was supplied, and the practical runtime severity depends on implementation-specific generated class hierarchies.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `BackboneElement` remains based on `Element`, but the new `BackboneType` artifact is based on `DataType` and defines the parallel `modifierExtension` branch for datatypes. The R6 package lists modifier-capable datatypes such as `Dosage`, `ElementDefinition`, `MarketingStatus`, `ProductShelfLife`, and `Timing` under `BackboneType` rather than `BackboneElement`.

facts.note: The artifact was not renamed or removed.
The direct base of BackboneElement did not change.
R6 introduces BackboneType with baseDefinition DataType.

R6 uses BackboneType for this datatype branch.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 `BackboneElement` artifacts match by canonical URL, id, name, type, kind, abstract flag, and direct base. The split was identified by the R6-only `BackboneType` StructureDefinition and by comparing StructureDefinition `baseDefinition` values across the local R4 and R6 packages.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a direct old-valid/new-invalid instance break: ordinary JSON/XML content does not carry the abstract base type name. It is a high runtime and code-generation risk because model libraries often expose abstract FHIR bases as classes, interfaces, or reflection metadata. Code that tests whether `Dosage`, `Timing`, or `ElementDefinition` is a `BackboneElement`, serializes all `BackboneElement` descendants through one branch, or derives profiles from the old base can fail or silently miss R6 datatype-side modifier extensions. For R6-to-R4 metadata conversion, `BackboneType` has no R4 counterpart, so converters must map the abstract hierarchy deliberately rather than copying it losslessly.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: No direct clinical data element changes were found in `BackboneElement`; the risk is primarily software compatibility. Safety impact could rise in a specific implementation if modifier extensions on datatype instances are skipped because of incorrect type dispatch.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate resource-contained backbone elements from datatypes that can carry modifier extensions while aligning datatype bases under DataType.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base-model design was identified that preserves the old BackboneElement inheritance while also making modifier-capable reusable datatypes part of the new DataType/BackboneType branch.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: the local definitions show `BackboneElement` still means elements inside resources, while R6 adds `DataType` and `BackboneType` so the few modifier-capable reusable datatypes can sit under a datatype branch. The break is mainly generated API, reflection, and StructureDefinition-conversion compatibility rather than old-valid/new-invalid instance content. Because FHIR StructureDefinition inheritance has a single formal `baseDefinition`, R6 could not both preserve the old `BackboneElement` ancestry for those datatypes and make them true `DataType`/`BackboneType` descendants. Without official change notes the rationale is inferred, so the calibrated verdict is `Probably justified` rather than fully `Justified`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The tempting less-disruptive designs are to leave the affected datatypes based on `BackboneElement`, or to make `BackboneType` a subtype or alias of `BackboneElement`. Those would preserve old `instanceof`, generated-base-class, and metadata-dispatch behavior, but they would fail the central R6 model goal: the datatype-side artifacts would still not be clean descendants of `DataType`, and the resource-backbone-versus-datatype distinction would remain blurred. A generated compatibility interface, alias, or converter mapping can still be useful migration support, but it is outside the normative base R6 StructureDefinition hierarchy and should not be counted as a backward-compatible base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping or aliasing BackboneElement would reduce generated-API churn but would retain the ambiguous datatype hierarchy; generated compatibility aliases are migration mitigations, not base-model alternatives.

evidence.detail: R4 BackboneElement is an abstract complex type derived from Element.
R6 BackboneElement remains an abstract complex type derived from Element.
R6 introduces BackboneType as an abstract complex type derived from DataType.
evidence.quote: Base definition for the few data types that are allowed to carry modifier extensions.

evidence.detail: The R4 package contains complex datatypes with baseDefinition BackboneElement, including Dosage, ElementDefinition, MarketingStatus, Population, ProdCharacteristic, ProductShelfLife, SubstanceAmount, and Timing.

The R6 package contains complex datatypes with baseDefinition BackboneType, including Dosage, DosageCondition, DosageDetails, DosageSafety, ElementDefinition, MarketingStatus, ProductShelfLife, RelativeTime, and Timing.

examples.examplesMd: Illustrative code-generation example: R4 generated APIs might allow `if (x instanceof BackboneElement)` to catch `Dosage` or `Timing`; R6 generated APIs should expect those datatype-side classes to derive from or implement `BackboneType` instead. This example is about generated runtime types, not a complete FHIR instance payload.

findings.narrativeMd: `BackboneElement` itself was not renamed and its local `modifierExtension` element did not change, but its practical inheritance role changed. In R4, several complex datatypes used `BackboneElement` as their formal base. In R6, those cases move to a new `BackboneType` branch. Implementers who only validate wire-format instances may see little difference, while implementers with generated class hierarchies or metadata-driven validators can encounter a real breaking API shift.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid resource fragment is not made invalid solely because `BackboneElement` split its datatype-side role; abstract base names are not serialized in normal instances. The compatibility risk appears when validators, serializers, or converters rely on StructureDefinition inheritance metadata. R6 metadata containing `BackboneType` is not directly representable in R4 because R4 has no `BackboneType` artifact; a cross-version converter must map it back to the older `BackboneElement`-based representation or to a compatibility abstraction.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit generated model base classes and any code that special-cases `BackboneElement`. In R6-aware code, route resource-contained backbone components through `BackboneElement` and modifier-capable datatype components through `BackboneType`. Cross-version StructureDefinition converters should include an explicit mapping between R4 datatype bases that used `BackboneElement` and R6 `BackboneType`. Regression tests should cover `Dosage`, `Timing`, and `ElementDefinition` because these are common infrastructure/datatype examples.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split was probably necessary to make the formal model match the semantic distinction already present in the `BackboneElement` definition. The less-breaking alternative would be a compatibility interface or alias so generated code could preserve old `BackboneElement` checks while still exposing `BackboneType`. That alternative reduces migration pain but risks preserving ambiguous hierarchy semantics.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official ballot migration notes if available. Also review concrete datatype reports because some affected datatypes changed for reasons beyond the abstract base split.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical `BackboneElement` identity, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and direct base are unchanged. The hierarchy-role split is recorded separately as a finding because R6 adds `BackboneType` for datatype-side use.
Both snapshots contain `BackboneElement`, `BackboneElement.id`, `BackboneElement.extension`, and `BackboneElement.modifierExtension`. The local differential remains root plus `modifierExtension`.
Root remains `0..*`; inherited `id` remains `0..1`; inherited `extension` and local `modifierExtension` remain `0..*`.
`id` remains FHIRPath string, and both `extension` and `modifierExtension` remain type `Extension`. No local choice-type addition or removal was found.
`BackboneElement` has no local Reference-typed element, so no target-profile change applies.
No terminology bindings are present on the local `BackboneElement` elements.

The local differential does not add or remove BackboneElement-owned constraints. Snapshot differences around `ele-1`, `condition`, XPath metadata, and whether `ext-1` is repeated on Extension-typed child elements are sourced to `Element` or `Extension` and are excluded from local findings.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value is present on the compared local elements.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue change was found.
`BackboneElement.modifierExtension` remains `isModifier=true` with the same modifier reason; root, `id`, and `extension` remain non-modifier.
`BackboneElement.modifierExtension` remains `isSummary=true`; inherited `id` and `extension` remain `isSummary=false` in the BackboneElement snapshot.
Inherited `BackboneElement.extension` slicing remains open by `url`; no local slicing is defined on `modifierExtension`.

The root short/definition are materially unchanged. `modifierExtension` wording is the same except for the spelling change `manageable` to `managable`, which does not appear to change conformance semantics.
No serialized element name, cardinality, XML attribute representation for `id`, or local type changed within the `BackboneElement` wire model.
Local `BackboneElement` instance content remains representable, but R6 `BackboneType` metadata has no R4 counterpart and must be handled by cross-version StructureDefinition conversion rules.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds generated narrative and package metadata around the same canonical artifact
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds or changes metadata such as generated narrative, `experimental=false`, jurisdiction, workgroup extension, publisher, and contact information. These do not change instance validation or the local element model.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that diff raw StructureDefinition JSON should filter publication metadata separately from computable model changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: modifierExtension definition has a spelling-only wording difference
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 text says `manageable`; the R6 text says `managable`. The surrounding normative statement, cardinality, type, modifier flag, summary flag, requirements, and aliases are otherwise unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Avoid treating exact prose-string comparison as a semantic break without reviewing the computable fields.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Inherited Extension invariant projection differs in the BackboneElement snapshot
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 snapshots repeated the Extension-sourced `ext-1` invariant on `BackboneElement.extension` and `BackboneElement.modifierExtension`; the R6 BackboneElement snapshot does not, while R6 `Extension` itself still carries `ext-1`. A validator that resolves the `Extension` type should still enforce the invariant.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Snapshot-only diff tools may report a false local relaxation. Attribute this to `Extension`/snapshot generation and verify validators resolve type constraints rather than relying only on the containing element constraint list.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `BackboneType` is the new abstract base created by the hierarchy split and should have its own report, including detailed comparison of its local `modifierExtension` model and downstream concrete datatype use.
`BackboneElement` inherits `id`, `extension`, and `ele-1` metadata from `Element`; those inherited changes should be assessed in the Element report rather than duplicated here.

`BackboneElement.extension` and `BackboneElement.modifierExtension` are typed as `Extension`. R6 changes to Extension's base, allowed value types, summary flags, and invariant projection can affect extension handling but are owned by the Extension report.
